The present claim petition has been filed by the petitioners against the respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/-
with interest for the death of Smt. M. R. Sangeetha in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 16-06-2024.

sentences.text: SCCH-10 2

. The case of the petitioners in brief is as under:
That, on 16.06.2024 at about 4.00 to 4.05 p.m., deceased M.R. Sangeetha was proceeding in the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-16-ER-5877 as a pillion rider and the same was ridden by her husband and while they were proceeding from Challekere to Hiriyur, near Gollahalli village, at that time, the driver of Ashok Leyland goods carrier bearing Reg. No.AP-02-TC-7819 came from opposite direction at high speed,
in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said motor cycle and caused the accident.
Due to the impact, the said M.R. Sangeetha who was proceeding in the said motor cycle fell down and sustained fatal injuries and died at the spot.

Petitioner No.1 is the husband and petitioner No.2 is minor daughter and they are the legal Maddegowda J vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17616383/
2 heirs of deceased.

sentences.text: Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, she was working as a Tailor and was earning Rs.25,000/- to 30,000/- per month.
Due to death of deceased, the petitioners have lost their source of income and are put to mental shock and agony.

Further, the accident was SCCH-10 occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Ashok Leyland Goods carrier bearing Reg.
No.AP-02- TC-7819.
As such, the respondent No.1 being insurer and respondent No.2 being owner are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

Hence, the petitioners prayed to award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/-
from the respondents under all heads together with interest and costs.

3. In response to the Petition notice, the respondent No.2 has not appeared before the Court,
remained absent and was placed exparte.
The respondent No.1 has appeared before the Court through its counsel and filed the written statement.
4. The contentions of the respondent No.1 in brief are as under:
The respondent No.1 contended that, the petition filed by the petitioners is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.
Further denied the entire petition averments.
The rash and negligent driving of the driver SCCH-10 of the offending vehicle is denied.
The accident and manner of accident are denied.
The income and avocation of the deceased was denied.
The owner of the offending vehicle has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
The compensation claimed is excessive and exorbitant.
On these main contentions, the respondent No.1 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that on 16.06.2024 at about 4.00 to 4.05 p.m., while Smt. M.R. Sangeetha was traveling as a pillion rider in a Motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-16-ER-5877 and when they reached near Gollahalli Village, Hiriyur Taluk,
Chitradurga District, at that time, the driver of the Ashoka Leyland Goods Carrier bearing Reg. No.AP-02-TC-7819 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against said Sangeetha, as a result, she fell down and sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the fatal injuries at the spot ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that, they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased M.R. Sangeetha ?
3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for SCCH-10 compensation as prayed?

If so,
at what rate and from whom?
4) What order or award?

 R E A S O N S 9. ISSUE No.1:

The petitioners have filed the present petition seeking compensation on account of death of Smt.
M.R. Sangeetha in a road traffic accident that occurred on 16-06-2024.
The SCCH-10 petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW-1.
Ex.P.1 is the FIR in crime No.102/2024 of Imangala PS and Ex.P.2 is the First information statement.

On perusal of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 it reveal that, I.O. has registered a case against the driver of Ashok Leyland goods carrier bearing Reg. No.AP-02-TC- 7819 for the commission of offences punishable under Section 279 and 304-A of IPC and Section 187 of MV Act.
Ex.P.8 is the charge sheet filed by the Imangala police against one Mr. Somareddy who is none other than the driver of offending vehicle.
Ex . P.6
and Ex
. P.7 are the Inquest mahazar and Postmortem report respectively.
On perusal of postmortem report, it reveals that the deceased died due to hyprolemic shock as a result of hemorrhage caused by the injuries suffered in the accident.

On perusal of the aforesaid documents, it is sufficient to conclude that, the accident in question had taken place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and deceased succumbed to the injuries due to the accident.
SCCH-10 10
. Besides, it is settled principles of law that, in a motor vehicles accident compensation cases strict proof of negligence is not required.

This view is supported by the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009(13) SCC page 530 in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs.
Himachalapradesh Road Transport Corporation and in AIR 2011 SC page 1504 in the case of Parameshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others.

No.AP-02-TC-7819 and the deceased Sangeetha succumbed to the fatal injuries due to the accident.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: In order to prove the relationship with the deceased, the petitioners have produced copies of Aadhaar cards as per Ex.P.10 to Ex.P.12.
On perusal of Ex.P.10 to Ex.P.12 it reveal that, the petitioner No.1 is the husband and petitioner No.2 is the daughter of deceased.
Further, the respondents have not so seriously disputed the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
Hence, I hold that the petitioners are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
13. ISSUE No.3:

It is the specific contention of the petitioners that, deceased Smt. Sangeetha. M.R was hale and healthy at the time of accident and she was working as a Tailor and was earning Rs.25,000/- to 30,000/- per month.
It is further contended that, due to untimely death of deceased they were put to great hardship and lost their bread earner of the family.
14. To prove the age of the deceased, the petitioners have SCCH-10 produced the Aadhaar card of the deceased as per Ex.P.10.
As per Ex.P.10, the date of birth of M. R. SAngeetha is shown as 01.01.1994.
The accident was occurred on 16.06.2024.
Therefore, at the time of accident, the deceased was aged 30 years.
15. Further, to prove the occupation and income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any document.
At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision reported in 2023(4) KCCR 3603 (DB) between Aneesahemmed Vs Mohammed Yusuf and Another.

sentences.text: In the above decision the Hon'ble High Court has taken into consideration the notional income as fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru (KSLSA in short).

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The KSLSA, Bengaluru as per letter dated 26.02.2022 - 01/NLA/2022/550/2022 has circulated the notional income chart prepared by them.
As per the said notional income chart, if the accident occurred in the year 2022, the notional income has to be taken as Rs.15,500/- per month.

Therefore, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble High Court and the SCCH-10 letter of KSLSA and also in the absence of proof of income, this Court is of the opinion that, if the notional income is taken into consideration for assessing the income of the deceased would be just and proper.
The accident was occurred on 16.06.2024.
Therefore, this Court has taken Rs.16,500/- as monthly income of the deceased.

16. Before proceeding to award compensation under the different heads, I feel it necessary to reproduce the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court rendered in Special Leave Petition (Civil)
No.25590/2014 in between National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors.

sentences.text: An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as necessary method of computation.
The established SCCH-10 income means the income minus the tax component.

(v) For determination of the multiplicand, the deduction for personal and living expenses, the tribunals and the courts shall be guided by paragraphs 30 to 32 of Sarla Verma which we have reproduced hereinbefore.
(vi) The selection of multiplier shall be as indicated in the Table in Sarla Verma read with paragraph 42 of that judgment.
(vii) The age of the deceased should be the basis for applying the multiplier.
(viii) Reasonable figures on conventional head, namely, loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
17. The age of the deceased is taken as 30 years at the time of accident for multiplier.

As per the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma and Ors Vs. Delhi Transport Corp. and Anr reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 an operative multiplier of 17 is applicable for the age group of 26 to 30 years.

sentences.text: 18. In the instant case, the deceased left behind her SCCH-10 husband (petitioner No.1) and her daughter (petitioner No.2) and they are dependents of the deceased.

In Sarla Verma case, the Hon'ble Apex Court has expressed the view regarding standardized deduction towards personal and living expenses, where the number of dependents are 2 to 3, the deduction would be 1/3rd.
As discussed supra, in the present case, petitioner No.1 (husband) and petitioner No.2 (minor daughter) of the deceased are the dependents.
Hence, in the present case, 1/3rd of the income of the deceased has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses.
In the present case, the Court has taken the view that the deceased was having monthly income of Rs.16,500/- and annual income would be Rs.1,98,000/-.

If 1/3rd is deducted towards personal expenses, the contribution to the family (dependents) is determined as Rs.1,32,000/-.
19.

As per Pranay Sethi case, if the deceased was self- employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the SCCH-10 deceased was under the age group of below 40 years.
In the present case, the deceased was aged 30 years at the time of accident and was on fixed salary.
Hence, an addition of 40% shall be added to Rs.1,32,000/-, it would be Rs.1,84,800/-.
The multiplier will be 17 having regard to the age of the deceased at the time of death (30 years).

Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.1,84,800/- X 17 =
Rs.31,41,600/-.
Thus, Rs.31,41,600/- is the compensation under the head of loss of dependency.

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 has specifically contended that, at the time of accident the charge sheeted driver had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the offending vehicle and hence the insured/owner of the offending vehicle has violated the terms and conditions of the policy and hence, the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation.
SCCH-10 26.

The learned counsel for respondent No.1 while canvassing the arguments has drawn my attention towards Ex.P.8 Charge sheet and submitted that, on the date of accident the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid driving licence and hence, I.O has invoked Section 3 R/w Section 181 of M.V. Act and hence, submitted that, the insurance company is not liable to pay compensation for the fundamental breach of policy condition.

27. In the instant case, as per the police records, the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid driving licence on the date of accident and hence, there is fundamental breach of policy condition.
Therefore, the respondent No.2 being the owner of the vehicle is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

28. The counsel for the petitioners has argued that, the petitioners are third party victims and though there is violation of policy condition if any, the insurance company has to satisfy the award amount and can recover the same from the owner.
SCCH-10 29.

It has been held by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in New India Assurance Co., Ltd., vs Yallavva W/O Yamanappa Dharnakeri in M.F.A. No. 30131 OF 2010 (MV-I) dated 12 May, 2020 that,
ii) The Insurer is liable to pay the third party and recover from the insured even if there is breach of any condition recognized under Section 149(2), even if it is a fundamental breach (that is breach of condition which is the cause for the accident) and the insurer proves the said breach in view of the mandate under Section 149(1) of the Act."

30. The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 would submit that, after the replacement of Section 149 of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 by Section 150 of Amendment Act 2019, the liability of the insurer to pay and its right to recover the amount from the owner has been taken away and hence, in the instant case, since the accident occurred after the said amendment, the Court cannot direct to pay compensation to the insurance company and to recover it from the owner.
SCCH-10 31.
In the instant case, though there is a violation of policy condition, the respondent No.1 has admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and same was in force on the date of accident.

The amendment to Section 149 of the Act will not take away the liability of the insurer to Maddegowda J vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17616383/

sentences.text: Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the insurer shall continue to indemnify the owner's risk in relation to the accident taking place after 01.04.2022 as Motor Vehicles Act is a Benevolent Legislation, the petitioners cannot be deprived of the compensation.

Therefore, in view of the valid insurance policy and indemnity between the respondents insured and insurer and in view of the above principles, at the first instance, the insurer i.e. respondent No.1 has to pay the award amount of Rs.32,73,600/- to the petitioners with interest @ 6% p.a. at the ratio of 40:60 from the date of petition till the date of deposit, then same has to be recovered from the respondent No.2/ owner of the offending vehicle in accordance with law.
Accordingly, I answer the SCCH-10 issue No.3 Partly in the affirmative.
32. Issue No.4:

In view of my finding on Issue No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.32,73,600/- with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. at the ratio of 40:60 respectively from the date of petition till realization of entire compensation awarded.

The respondent No.1 insurance company is liable to pay compensation amount as awarded to the petitioners and directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest within 30 days as contemplated under Sec.168(3) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
The respondent No.1 / insurance company is at liberty to recover the compensation amount from the owner/ respondent No.2 in accordance with law.
SCCH-10

Out of the award amount, 40% of the award amount of petitioner No.1 shall be invested in fixed deposit for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank of petitioner's choice and balance amount shall be released in the name of petitioner No.1 through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.
The entire amount with accrued interest awarded to petitioner No.2 shall be deposited in any nationalized or schedule bank till she attains the age of majority.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
Draw award accordingly.
